title: netinf-guide
text: netinf identifies influential cases psychological network analysis. network analysis, often care “cases largest impact results?” example, removing case, global strength, centrality ranking, even sign edge change? netinf strings diagnostic steps together coherent workflow. package contains following three main parts: Core components: extracting case indices bootstrap samples → computing empirical influence values → leave-one-validation → computing centrality gCD --one function: influence_diagnostic() performs one call Visualization: three plot functions

title: netinf-guide
text: Overview Step 1: bootnet_with_indices Step 2: calculate_empirical_influence Step 3: leave_one_out_analysis Step 4: calculate_centrality_gCD --one: influence_diagnostic influence_plot gcds_plot gcds_md_plot

text: netinf designed bottom-pipeline: can run step manually, use influence_diagnostic() run four steps one call.

what: What bootstrap does in network analysis
title: netinf-guide
text: core network analysis estimating network structure (e.g., partial correlation network, GLASSO network). stable estimated network? standard approach bootstrap: draw nn cases replacement original data re-estimate network. Repeating BB times gives us BB “resampled networks”, can use assess confidence intervals edge weights, stability centrality, . Mathematically, bb-th bootstrap sample : X(b)={xi1(b),xi2(b),…,xin(b)} X^{(b)} = \{x_{i_1^{(b)}}, x_{i_2^{(b)}}, \dots, x_{i_n^{(b)}}\} ik(b)∈{1,2,…,n}i_k^{(b)} \\{1, 2, \dots, n\} case index drawn replacement original data.

previous_headings: The core idea: why we need case indices
what: The problem: bootnet does not store these indices by default
title: netinf-guide
text: default, bootnet::bootnet() uses memorysaver = TRUE. save memory, store bootstrap data, sampling indices ik(b)i_k^{(b)}. compute “empirical influence” case—measures much case influences results via inclusion frequency—must know cases drawn bootstrap sample.

previous_headings: The core idea: why we need case indices
title: netinf-guide
text: bootnet_with_indices() three things: Calls bootnet::bootnet() memorysaver = FALSE, data bootstrap sample retained Recovers original case indices row names bootstrap dataset default, uses keep_data = FALSE discard data immediately indices extracted, saving memory returned object bootnetWithIndices object: bootnet result additional object bootIndices.

title: netinf-guide
text: use simulated dataset based 9 variables HolzingerSwineford1939 dataset lavaan.
code: library(netinf) set.seed(123) dat <- lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939 datused <- dat[, paste0("x", 1:9)]  #Following Fried's suggestion(2017),N/P > 10 sample_idx <- sample(1:nrow(datused), 99) data_99 <- datused[sample_idx, ] means_99 <- colMeans(data_99) sds_99 <- sapply(data_99, sd) case_100 <- numeric(9)  #One influential case names(case_100) <- paste0("x", 1:9) high_vars <- c("x1", "x2", "x4", "x6", "x7", "x3", "x5", "x8", "x9") case_100 <- means_99 case_100[high_vars] <- means_99[high_vars] + 2 * sds_99[high_vars] data <- rbind(data_99, case_100)

title: netinf-guide
text: addition bootnet objects (sample, boots, sampleTable, bootTable, etc.), one extra object “bootIndices”: bootIndices[[b]] vector length nn. kk-th element indicates row original data drawn position kk bb-th bootstrap sample. indices input calculate_empirical_influence(), turns numeric influence value per case.
code: class(boot_res) #> [1] "bootnetWithIndices" "bootnet" names(boot_res) #> [1] "sampleTable" "bootTable"   "sample"      "boots"       "type"        #> [6] "sampleSize"  "bootIndices" # The case indices drawn in each bootstrap sample length(boot_res$bootIndices)      # equals nBoots #> [1] 5000 str(boot_res$bootIndices[[1]])    # indices from the first bootstrap #>  num [1:100] 68 39 1 34 87 43 14 82 59 51 ...

title: netinf-guide
text: bootstrap network, compute global strength(sum absolute edge weights): GS(b)=∑j<k|wjk(b)| \text{GS}^{(b)} = \sum_{j < k} |w_{jk}^{(b)}| wjk(b)w_{jk}^{(b)} edge weight nodes jj kk bb-th bootstrap network.

previous_headings: Step 2: calculate_empirical_influence > Why this step exists
title: netinf-guide
text: case ii bootstrap sample bb, let: ci(b)=number times case appears bootstrap sample b c_i^{(b)} = \text{number times case } \text{ appears bootstrap sample } b exactly information stored bootIndices[[b]] (frequency table).

previous_headings: Step 2: calculate_empirical_influence > Why this step exists
title: netinf-guide
text: fit linear model: GS(b)=β0+∑=1nβi⋅ci(b)+ε(b) \text{GS}^{(b)} = \beta_0 + \sum_{=1}^{n} \beta_i \cdot c_i^{(b)} + \varepsilon^{(b)} coefficient empirical influence βi\beta_i measures much case ii contributes global strength.

previous_headings: Step 2: calculate_empirical_influence > Why this step exists
title: netinf-guide
text: Drop one case avoid collinearity. Since ∑ici(b)=n\sum_i c_i^{(b)} = n every bb, inclusion counts perfectly collinear intercept. function drops case 1 sets influence value via sum--zero constraint. Center mean zero. estimating β1,…,βn\beta_1, \dots, \beta_n, values centered: β̃=βi−1n∑j=1nβj \tilde{\beta}_i = \beta_i - \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j=1}^{n} \beta_j  average influence 0. Positive values mean “including case increases global strength”; negative values mean opposite.

title: netinf-guide
text: large positive value case ii means: Including case ii sample tends increase global strength. large negative value means: Including case ii tends decrease global strength. Note: values regression coefficients. regression, case’s inclusion proportion bootstrap sample ranges 0 (never drawn) 1 (always drawn). coefficient case ii therefore quantifies: much predicted global strength changes case ii’s inclusion proportion moves 0 1, holding cases constant regression sense. hypothetical 0--1 change—single bootstrap sample proportions sum 1, case can independently reach 1. values meaningful ranking cases within analysis. measure actual change global strength, use leave_one_out_analysis() (see Step 3), physically removes case re-estimates network. ## Possible pitfalls

title: netinf-guide
text: nBoots small, regression may stable. Roughly speaking, 5000+ good.

title: netinf-guide
text: bootstrap networks almost global strength (e.g., network nearly empty), response variable almost zero variance regression may fails nBoots small.

title: netinf-guide
text: empirical influence values identify candidate influential cases—large absolute coefficient. next function, leave_one_out_analysis(), validates candidates actually removing data re-estimating network, one case time (several specifying remove_cases).

title: netinf-guide
text: confirm candidate truly matters, need actually remove data, re-estimate network, see changes. leave_one_out_analysis() .

title: netinf-guide
text: core operation simple: take data, remove one several cases, re-estimate network, compare full-sample network. single case ii: Ĝ(−)=estimateNetwork(X\{xi}) \hat{G}^{(-)} = \text{estimateNetwork}(X \setminus \{x_i\}) set cases SS: Ĝ(−S)=estimateNetwork(X\{xi:∈S}) \hat{G}^{(-S)} = \text{estimateNetwork}(X \setminus \{x_{} : \S\}) function supports : Single-case removal: remove one case time compare result full network. classic leave-one-(LOO) design returns object class looAnalysis. Multi-case removal: remove several cases simultaneously compare resulting network full network. leave-multiple-(LMO) design returns object class looMultiAnalysis. multi-case design also useful suspect several cases act jointly—combined effect may differ sum individual effects, especially correlated share common pattern. removed case set, re-estimated network Ĝ(−)\hat{G}^{(-)} (Ĝ(−S)\hat{G}^{(-S)}) compared full-sample network Ĝ\hat{G} several dimensions: Global strength: much sum absolute edge weights change? Edges disappeared: present Ĝ\hat{G}, zero Ĝ(−)\hat{G}^{(-)}? Edges appeared: zero Ĝ\hat{G}, present Ĝ(−)\hat{G}^{(-)}? Edges reversed sign: edge opposite direction?

title: netinf-guide
text: function needs know cases remove. Supply one three options: remove_cases (manual IDs), threshold (select magnitude), top_n (select top N magnitude). none supplied, function defaults cases one supplied, priority remove_cases > threshold > top_n, warning tells arguments ignored.

title: netinf-guide
text: threshold top_n, direction argument controls tail influence distribution select: "": use |influence||\text{influence}| (default) "positive": cases increase global strength "negative": cases decrease global strength

title: netinf-guide
text: One case removed time (remove_cases length 1, threshold / top_n produce one candidate): returns looAnalysis Multiple cases removed simultaneously (remove_cases length > 1): returns looMultiAnalysis

title: netinf-guide
text: given centrality measure (Strength, Closeness, Betweenness), let θ=(θ1,θ2,…,θp) \theta = (\theta_1, \theta_2, \dots, \theta_p) vector centrality values across pp nodes, computed full-sample network. Similarly, let θ(−)=(θ1(−),θ2(−),…,θp(−)) \theta^{(-)} = (\theta_1^{(-)}, \theta_2^{(-)}, \dots, \theta_p^{(-)}) centrality vector removing case ii.

title: netinf-guide
text: Define difference: di=θ−θ(−) d_i = \theta - \theta^{(-)}

title: netinf-guide
text: bootstrap networks (boot_result$boots), compute centrality vector sample: θ(1),θ(2),…,θ(B) \theta^{(1)}, \theta^{(2)}, \dots, \theta^{(B)} estimate covariance: V=Cov(θ(1),…,θ(B))∈ℝp×p V = \mathrm{Cov}(\theta^{(1)}, \dots, \theta^{(B)}) \\mathbb{R}^{p \times p}

text: gCD case ii squared Mahalanobis distance did_i: gCDi=di⊤V−1di \text{gCD}_i = d_i^\top V^{-1} d_i

title: Calculate Generalized Cook's Distance for Centrality Measures — calculate_centrality_gCD
text: centrality measure, covariance matrix node-level centrality values estimated bootstrap samples stored boot_result$boots. gCD case \(\) computed $$gCD_i = (\theta - \theta_{(-)})' V^{-1} (\theta - \theta_{(-)})$$ \(\theta\) vector centrality values full sample, \(\theta_{(-)}\) vector removing case \(\), \(V\) bootstrap covariance matrix. \(V\) singular, Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse MASS::ginv() used.
